title: Etale localization of the ambient adjoint
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For a separated etale morphism $u:U\to X$ of finite type [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], etale sum extension $u_!$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] is exact on sheaves, and its termwise derived functor is left adjoint to $u^*$ on these whole derived categories. For the compact-support assertion assume in addition that $A$ is finite. If $f:X\to S$ and $fu:U\to S$ are compactifiable morphisms between Noetherian schemes [def-asd-compactifiable, def-amb-etale-compact-support], and $f^\times,(fu)^\times$ denote their ordinary etale compact-support right adjoints [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], then for every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$u^*f^\times K\cong(fu)^\times K.$$
The notation refers only to ordinary etale compact supports.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] to the constant ring $A$: the sum-extension functor defined in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] is exact and satisfies $u_!\dashv u^*$ on module sheaves. The inverse-image functor is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. These assertions hold for every commutative ring $A$.

Both exact functors descend termwise to the entire unbounded derived categories by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. By [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], their sheaf unit and counit give a complex adjunction. Descend these transformations by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Their triangle identities hold after precomposition with localization, since they hold degreewise; clause (3) of the same node implies the identities on the derived categories. This proves $Du_!\dashv u^*$ with no boundedness assumption.

For the compact-support assertion assume $A$ finite, and let $f:X\to S$ and $fu:U\to S$ be compactifiable morphisms between Noetherian schemes, so $U$, $X$ and $S$ are Noetherian. Then $u$ is a separated etale morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes, and [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] applies to it. For every compactification $U\xrightarrow{j}\overline U\xrightarrow{r}X$ of $u$ it gives a canonical natural isomorphism $c_{u,(j,r)}:Rr_*Dj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Du_!$ on all unbounded complexes. Here $Rr_*Dj_!$ is the candidate of [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and $Du_!$ is the degreewise descent of step 2. Its degree-zero sheaf map sends a section with support proper over an etale test object to its components on the etale sheets. These isomorphisms agree under the proper-refinement comparisons normalized to be the identity over $U$. They carry the compact-support adjunction of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] for $u$ to $Du_!\dashv u^*$, including its sum/evaluation counit. No particular compactification of $u$ is chosen here; step 5 supplies one.

proof.text: Obtain unbounded refinement comparisons directly from [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange]. Let $h:Z\to B$ be a compactifiable morphism of Noetherian schemes, and let $q:T_1\to T_2$ be a proper refinement of compactifications $(j_1,r_1),(j_2,r_2)$ of $h$, with $qj_1=j_2$ and $r_1=r_2q$. Use the interchange square with left proper map $\mathrm{id}_Z$, right proper map $q$, and top and bottom opens $j_1,j_2$. It gives $Dj_{2!}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*Dj_{1!}$. Apply $Rr_{2*}$ and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to compare $Rr_{2*}Dj_{2!}$ with $Rr_{1*}Dj_{1!}$. Vertical pasting in the interchange node proves compatibility with composite refinements and identities. All ambient compactifications are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], as their proper maps to the Noetherian target are finite type. The cofiltered category in [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered] now identifies any two candidates canonically: choose a common refinement and compose one comparison with the inverse of the other. Two choices have a common further refinement, where the composite identities just proved make these maps equal; the same argument for three objects gives the cocycle identity. Since the left edge is $\mathrm{id}_Z$, these are the refinement comparisons normalized to be the identity over $Z$, so for $h=u$ the isomorphisms of step 3 are compatible with them.

source.place: Tags 0F7B case (b), 0F7C, 0F7I: proper-refinement comparisons on unbounded inputs

proof.text:
For composable compactifiable maps $Z\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{g}B$, choose compactifications $Y\xrightarrow{i}\overline Y\xrightarrow{s}B$ of $g$ and $Z\xrightarrow{a_0}W\xrightarrow{t}B$ of $gh$. By [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] choose a compatible tower $Z\xrightarrow{a}\overline Z\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$ and put $V=\overline Z\times_{\overline Y}Y$, with open $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline Z$, proper $q:V\to Y$, and open $j:Z\hookrightarrow V$, so $bj=a$. The ambient schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; $V$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The proper/open isomorphism $Di_!Rq_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*Db_!$ of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] gives
$$Rg_!Rh_!=Rs_*Di_!Rq_*Dj_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs_*Rp_*Db_!Dj_!\cong R(sp)_*Da_!=R(gh)_!.$$
The last identification uses [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the degreewise descent of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition], justified by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Every arrow is defined on unbounded complexes over the finite ring $A$. Take $h=u$ and $g=f$, with $(i,s)$ the compactification of $f$ used for $f^\times$ and $(a_0,t)$ the compactification of $fu$ used for $(fu)^\times$. The tower supplies a proper $v:\overline Z\to W$ with $va=a_0$ and $tv=sp$, so step 4 identifies $R(sp)_*Da_!$ with $Rt_*Da_{0!}$. Precompose with $Rs_*Di_!$ of the inverse of $c_{u,(j,q)}$ from step 3 for the compactification $(j,q)$ of $u$ produced by the tower. This gives $c_M:Rf_!Du_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}R(fu)_!M$.

The composition calculation is canonical under the comparisons of step 4. Indeed two towers have a common refining tower by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]; its comparison diagram consists of proper/open squares. Vertical pasting for [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] says that inserting a proper refinement before the tower interchange equals inserting it after. Horizontal pasting says that combining its two open arrows agrees with their composite. These are precisely the two ways around the comparison diagram for the displayed chain in step 5, so that chain is independent of tower. For three factors, the same two pasting identities identify each parenthesized chain with the chain for the outer rectangles. The direct-image identifications [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] are the canonical ones on resolutions, and the open-extension identifications [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] are associative; hence composition is associative. The isomorphisms $c_{u,(j,q)}$ of step 3 agree under refinement comparisons, so the inverse inserted in step 5 is unchanged when the tower is refined; hence $c_M$ is independent of the tower. For two etale maps their iterated sheaf sum sends a nested lift and its section to the composite lift and the same section; this agrees with the composite adjunction counit, which evaluates that section. This also fixes the etale composition normalization.

proof.text:
For $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, step 2, [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and $c_M$ give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_U(M,u^*f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Du_!M,f^\times K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Rf_!Du_!M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(R(fu)_!M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_U(M,(fu)^\times K).$$
Send the identity on $u^*f^\times K$ through these bijections to define $e_K:u^*f^\times K\to(fu)^\times K$. Using the inverse bijections on the other identity defines its inverse: naturality in $M$ makes both composites identities. Naturality in $K$ gives the asserted natural isomorphism. The adjoint theorem applies because $f$ and $fu$ are compactifiable between Noetherian schemes and $A$ is finite.

source.place: Paragraph 2, displayed Hom calculation and Yoneda

proof.text:
Write $L=u^*f^\times K$. The transpose of $e_K$ is exactly
$$R(fu)_!L\xrightarrow{c_L^{-1}}Rf_!Du_!L\xrightarrow{Rf_!(\varepsilon^u_{f^\times K})}Rf_!f^\times K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^f_K}K.$$
This identifies the counit normalization; the corresponding unit is the transpose under the same Hom bijections, and its triangle identities are those of the two adjunctions. For further etale $v:W\to U$, the composite sum-extension adjunction has counit $\varepsilon^u\circ Du_!(\varepsilon^v)$. The direct and iterated Hom bijections therefore compose with the same two evaluation counits and $\varepsilon^f$, by step 6's associativity and etale normalization. They agree for every $M$, so applying them to the identities gives the same direct and iterated locality isomorphisms.

blueprint_update.statement:
For a separated etale morphism $u:U\to X$ of finite type,
$u_!$ is exact and is left adjoint to $u^*$ on the whole
ordinary derived categories. If $f$ and $fu$ are
compactifiable, there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
u^*f^\times K\cong(fu)^\times K.
$$

proof.text:
An etale morphism is a local homeomorphism of etale topoi.
For an etale test object $V\to X$, the sheaf $u_!F$
consists of sections on $U\times_XV$ with support proper
over $V$; after an etale covering which separates any finite
set of support points, this is the direct sum of the sections on
the corresponding sheets. This description is independent of
the covering by sheaf descent. It gives
$(u_!F)_{\bar x}=\bigoplus_{\bar z\in U_{\bar x}}F_{\bar z}$,
so $u_!$ is exact. Maps from these sums to $G$ are
precisely maps $F\to u^*G$, first on separated sheets and
then by sheaf descent. Thus $u_!\dashv u^*$ already on
sheaves. Both functors are exact, so the adjunction descends
termwise to ordinary derived categories.

For any complex $M$ on $U$, use the ambient adjunction
of [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] and the composition
of compact supports in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]:

$$
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Hom}_U(M,u^*f^\times K)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(u_!M,f^\times K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(Rf_!u_!M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(R(fu)_!M,K).
\end{split}
$$

Yoneda gives the displayed isomorphism and its compatibility
with units, counits, and further etale localization.
